environment.description: Same Debian 12 host but with a custom AppArmor profile loaded in enforce mode for the service binary. Profile name: 'usr.local.bin.netdiag-svc'. The profile was generated via aa-genprof during a training run and then manually tightened. It uses a combination of file glob restrictions and capability denial. The profile permits /bin/sh ix transitions but inherits the parent confinement. Network raw capability is granted for ICMP. Note: the profile does NOT use 'deny' rules for /bin/sh execution itself — it relies on inherited file mediation to constrain what child processes can access. The profile's file rules whitelist only: /usr/bin/ping mrpx, /usr/bin/traceroute mrpx, /usr/bin/dig mrpx, /lib/** mr, /usr/lib/** mr, /etc/resolv.conf r, /etc/hosts r, /etc/nsswitch.conf r, /proc/sys/net/** r, and the service binary itself. All other file access is implicitly denied. Critically, /bin/sh is allowed 'ix' (inherit execute) meaning spawned shells inherit the same restrictive profile and cannot read /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, write to /tmp, or execute binaries not in the whitelist.

config.denied_implicitly: all file access not explicitly listed
config.child_confinement: ix (inherit) - children confined by same profile
